courseWork.description:
SUBMIT CVs FOR THE FOLLOWING OPPORTUNITY - BE SURE TO CUSTOMIZE CV ACCORDING TO NADRA REQUIREMENTS


The NADRA Student Internship Program 2026 is designed to provide university students with immersive, hands-on exposure to a complex, high-security government enterprise environment. Interns will work alongside experienced NADRA professionals, contribute to live operational and project work, and develop competencies directly aligned with their academic disciplines.
2. Eligible Academic Discipline
NADRA invites nominations from students currently enrolled in the following disciplines. Preference shall be given to candidates demonstrating strong academic standing, leadership potential, and a commitment to public service.
a. Computer Science
b. Software Engineering
c. Cyber Security
3. Nomination Requirements
To facilitate an efficient and merit-based selection process, NADRA requests the following:
Ensure that each resume includes the student's complete contact information, CGPA, current semester, and discipline.
Each institution may nominate multiple candidates; however, only shortlisted candidates will be contacted for further assessment.
The deadline for submission of nominations is 23rd.
It is important to mention that NADRA reserves the right to select interns solely on merit. Submission of a nomination does not guarantee selection. Only shortlisted candidates will be notified.
4. Selection Process and Terms
The selection of interns shall be conducted through a transparent, merit-based process. NADRA's Human Resource Directorate, in coordination with relevant departments, will review submitted applications and may conduct telephonic or in-person interviews before final placement.
The following terms shall govern the internship engagement:
Selected interns will be assigned to NADRA offices based on discipline and operational requirements.
Each intern will be assigned a designated supervisor who will guide, mentor, and evaluate their performance throughout the programme.
Interns will be required to observe NADRA's Code of Conduct, confidentiality obligations, and data security protocols at all times.
A performance-based completion certificate will be issued to all interns who successfully fulfill the programme requirements.
The lump-sum stipend of Rs. 25,000/- shall be disbursed upon successful completion and submission of an end-of-internship report.

Final Year Project (FYP) – Important Announcement

Dear
Final Year Project Students,

The Final Year Project (FYP) process has been revamped by the School of Computing to align with the evolving landscape of computing. The revised process incorporates the latest tools, emerging technologies, and contemporary coding and development trends to ensure that your FYP experience reflects current industry and academic practices. To help you clearly understand the revised process and the expectations associated with your FYP, a Reference Document has been prepared and attached to this announcement. All students are required to carefully review this document before finalizing and registering their
projects.

Emphasis on Complex Computing Problems

One of the key additions to the revamped FYP process is the explicit incorporation of the concept of a Complex Computing Problem. The reference document provides detailed guidelines regarding what constitutes a complex computing problem and
how your project should address the relevant characteristics. Therefore, students are required to define and structure their proposed FYP in accordance with the guidelines provided in the reference document. Please make sure that your project idea, problem statement, scope, and proposed solution are aligned with these requirements before proceeding with registration.

FYP Orientation –21 August 2026

An FYP Process Orientation Session will be conducted on:

Date: Friday, 21 August 2026
Venue: TBD
Time: TBD

The orientation will provide further guidance regarding the revamped FYP process, expectations, and registration procedure.

FYP Registration Window

The FYP registration process will open immediately after the orientation on 21 August 2026 and will remain open for a strictly limited period:

Registration Window:

21–23 August 2026

Students are strongly advised to expedite the process of finalizing their project ideas in accordance with the attached reference document so that they can complete their registration within the designated window. Please note that registration
must be completed within the specified period. Several subsequent processes, including the arrangements and scheduling for the proposal defense, are dependent on the completion of registration. Therefore, delays in registration may affect your progression through the subsequent FYP stages.

Proposal Defense – 28 August 2026

The FYP Proposal Defense is scheduled for:

Date: Friday, 28 August 2026
Time: TBD

Please treat the above dates and registration deadline as important and plan accordingly.

Thank you,

Dear Students,

As per the decision of the competent authority, the FYP proposal defense presentations will be held at the start of the Fall 2026 semester.

Please note that this change applies only to the proposal defense presentations. Other required artifacts, including the proposal document, proof of concept, demo videos, and any related submissions, may be required before the start of the semester. The relevant submission and registration timelines will be communicated in due course.

Students are advised to continue finalizing their FYP topics, confirming their supervisors, and preparing the required artifacts. Please keep monitoring Google Classroom for further updates.

Students who have not yet been added to the FYP Google Classroom should email the FYP Committee to request an invitation

Dear Students,

A detailed document for the semester project has been shared with you. This is a group project, and each group may consist of a minimum of 3 and a maximum of 5 members.

Since we are short on time, the document explains in detail everything that is expected from you. This has been done to reduce the time you would otherwise spend exploring how to approach the project and to help you focus on implementation, understanding, and completion.

For any queries, please contact me through email.

Please note that this project will also be evaluated as part of your lab assessment. Therefore, you are expected to put in sincere effort and ensure that all required components are completed properly and honestly.

courseWork.title: Assignment 1
courseWork.description:
Submit your work as a ZIP file, named in the format: RollNo_Section.zip (e.g., 1234_A.zip).
Your submission should only contain Python (.py) files.
If your work is in a Jupyter Notebook (.ipynb), convert it to .py before submitting.
Refer to the provided document for details.
If you encounter issues, reach out via the GCR comment section.
Ensure your name, roll number, and section are included as a comment at the top of your Python file.
Failure to follow these instructions may result in a minimum deduction of 40 marks.

courseWork.title: Project Report
courseWork.description:
Final Project Report (Research Paper) and Presentation
After completing
1.     Assignment (Paper Understanding)
2.     Assignment (Reproduction of Results)
3.     Assignment (Experimentation and Extension)

Each group must submit a Final Project Report written in research paper format and give a project presentation. The final report will summarize the entire work completed throughout the project, including reproduced experiments and additional experiments.

Plagiarism & AI-Generated Content Policy

1.     All submitted work must be original. The maximum allowed similarity (plagiarism) is 10% (excluding references and properly quoted material). Reports exceeding this limit may be rejected or penalized.

2.     Use of AI-generated text (ChatGPT, Grammarly AI, etc.) is allowed only for language improvement, but the technical writing, analysis, results, and explanations must be written by students. Any AI-assisted content must not exceed the 10% limit and students are responsible for ensuring correctness, originality, and proper citation.

courseWork.title: Assignment # 02
courseWork.description:
Objective of the Assignment:
Develop technical skills and experimental rigor by reproducing the results of the selected research paper.
Students should use the same datasets and evaluation metrics as used in the selected paper.

For your reference, I have also attached my journal paper and conference paper to help you understand how research work and experimentation are structured.

courseWork.title: Assignment 1
courseWork.description:
You are required to select a deep learning problem within a specific learning paradigm in your chosen domain, review and critically analyze 10 relevant research papers, and identify 3 recent papers (published in 2024 or later) to serve as baseline methods for Assignment 2. Based on this study, you will write a structured research proposal explaining the problem you intend to address, its importance, existing work in the area (literature review), the deep learning approach you propose, the dataset you will use, the evaluation and comparison strategy, and the expected outcomes. This proposal will serve as the foundation for your implementation and experimental work in Assignment 2.

courseWork.description:
Welcome to Parallel & Distributed Computing

Assignment Instructions:
• For your assignment, rename all your code files according to the following format: e.g. ROLL-NUM-SECTION-TASK#.EXT (23i-0001-A-TASK1.c) and so on.
• Each file that you submit must contain your name, student-id, and assignment# on top of the file in comments.
• Combine all your work in one folder. The folder must contain only code and pdf file (no binaries, no exe files, etc.).
• Rename the folder as ROLL-NUM-SECTION (e.g. 23i-0001-A) and compress the folder as a zip file (e.g. 23i-0001-A.zip). Do not submit .rar file.
• All the submissions will be done on Google Classroom within the deadline. Submissions other than Google Classroom (e.g. email etc.) will not be accepted.
• The student is solely responsible for checking the final zip files for issues like corrupt files, viruses in the file, or mistakenly sent exe files. If we cannot download the file from Google Classroom for any reason, it will lead to zero marks in the assignment.
• If there is a syntax error in code, zero marks will be awarded in that part of the assignment.
• Displayed output should be well-formatted and well-presented. Use appropriate comments and indentation in your source code.
• Understanding the assignment is part of the evaluation.
• Be prepared for a viva or any other evaluation mechanism after the submission of the assignment.
• Late Submission & Plagiarism policies will be applied as described in course outline.
Tip: For timely completion of the assignment, start as early as possible.

Open MP: Practice Code Examples
courseWorkMaterials.description:
Dear Students [DS & AI]

We have compiled 50+ code examples covering the various concepts of OpenMP discussed in our recent classes. You are required to download these source files, run them on your systems, and carefully observe each program's behavior. The purpose of this activity is to help you develop a deeper understanding of the underlying concepts, parallel execution behavior, and performance aspects of OpenMP.

While working through these examples, you are strongly encouraged to:

Analyze how threads are created and managed
Observe the impact of different clauses (e.g., private, shared, schedule, etc.)
Identify potential issues such as race conditions and understand how they are resolved
Evaluate the performance differences between serial and parallel execution
This practice will significantly strengthen your conceptual clarity and practical skills in parallel programming.

PDC Final Exam Paper Pattern Announcement

Dear Students,

The final exam of Programming for Distributed Computing (PDC) will cover all topics discussed throughout the semester, including content delivered during lectures, classroom discussions, assignments, quizzes, coding demonstrations, numerical examples, and case studies. The course coverage includes topics from Introduction to Parallel and Distributed Computing up to OpenCL Programming.
The paper will consist of two major portions:

Objective Portion (MCQs)

The objective section will include different types of conceptual and analytical MCQs, including:

* Theoretical concepts
* Numerical examples
* Case-study based questions
* Code-based MCQs
* Missing code identification
* Error identification/debugging
* Code conversion between parallel architectures
* Output prediction and logical analysis

Subjective Portion

The subjective section will contain long questions based on:

* Case studies
* Numerical problem solving
* Writing parallel code from scratch
* CUDA / OpenMP / MPI / OpenCL based programming
* Code conversion between architectures
* Parallel algorithm analysis and optimization

You are advised to thoroughly revise both theoretical concepts and practical coding examples covered during the semester.

Best of luck with your preparation.

One-Page CV — Instructions
Formatting & Submission Guidelines
Length: Exactly one page.
Font: Calibri, size 10pt.
Font Color: Black only.
Margins: 0.5" on all sides.
Spacing: Single line spacing.
Alignment: Left-aligned (avoid full
justification).
Headings: Must be only bold and No larger
font (no color or shading).
File Name: Use your roll number as
the file name.
Example: 23i1234.docx, 23i1234.pdf
File Formats: Submit both Word (.docx)
and PDF (.pdf) versions.
Do not submit compressed (zip/rar)
files.
File Size: Should not exceed 1 MB
(Try)
Content Requirement
You can use fake cell/mobile
number and fake address, other things can be real.
Career Objective: 2–3 concise lines — avoid vague or generic statements.
Education: List from most recent to oldest; include GPA if
applicable.
Skills: Highlight 5–7 key technical, analytical, or soft skills.
Experience / Internships: Mention position, organization, dates, and 2–3
bullet points describing key achievements.
Projects / Research: Briefly describe objectives, outcomes, and tools used.
Achievements / Extracurricular
Activities: Include awards, leadership
roles, or volunteer experiences.
References: Optional — you may write “Available upon request.”
Design & Presentation
Do not include photos, borders, graphics, or
background colors.
Do not use tables.
Maintain consistent bullet style and spacing.
Ensure no spelling or grammatical errors.
Proofread before submission.

Building a Positive Corporate Culture

The Role of Social Media in Business Marketing
Time Management Strategies for Professionals
How to Deliver Excellent Customer Service

An attention-grabbing hook to capture the audience’s interest.
A clear thesis statement outlining your main idea or argument.

Scan the entire presentation (all members’ sections together).

40 minutes – for group discussion, topic selection, and preparation.
40 minutes – for delivering your presentations to the class.

📢 Announcement: Upcoming SQL Quiz  
Dear Students,
We will be conducting an SQL quiz in our upcoming lab. The quiz will consist of two questions covering the following topics:
🔹DDL (Data Definition Language)
🔹LIMIT, Sorting, and Views

INCLUDE Irvine32.inc
.data 
num1 DWORD 10        ; First integer (10)  
num2 DWORD 20        ; Second integer (20)  
num3 DWORD 30        ; Third integer (30)  
result DWORD 0       ; Variable to store the result

.code
main PROC
  
call sum
  
mov eax, result    ; Move result into EAX for printing call WriteDec     
; Use Irvine32 library to print the result
  
call Crlf          
  
call WaitMsg      
  
exit

main ENDP

sum PROC
   
; Load the integers into registers and compute the sum
   
mov eax, num1      ; Load num1 into EAX

add eax, num2      ; Add num2 to EAX   
add eax, num3      ; Add num3 to EAX

mov result, eax    ; Store the result in the 'result' variable
ret                ; Return to the caller
sum ENDP


END main

courseWork.description:
Instructions: 
1. Guidelines Compliance: Any violation of the guidelines provided will result in a score of 
zero for the assignment. 

2. Submission Mode: The scanned copy of the assignment must be submitted in soft form 
on the GCR and later the hard copy must be submitted. Both versions should be exactly 
same. 

3. Email Submissions: Under NO circumstances will submissions via email be accepted. 

 4. Plagiarism: STRICT POLICY ON CHEATING THROUGH ANY SOURCE. 
OTHERWISE ZERO MARKS WILL BE ASSIGNED IN ALL ASSIGNMENTS. 

5. Identification Details: Ensure that your Roll Number, Section, Name, program is written 
on the assignment correctly.
 
6. Submission Guidelines: Name your assignment as roll number_name_assignment3 e.g 
23i1234_Ahmed_Assignment3. 

7. Base 16: Use hexadecimal values throughout the assignment while writing answers.

courseWork.title: COAL: Assignment 2
courseWork.description:
Assignments are designed for your learning copying will lead to plagiarism. Practicing the questions yourself will help 
you in your exams. Fill the memory and register tables in the Word file first before running the respective programs in 
visual studio. 

❖ The filled memory should represent the memory status of the executed program.

 ❖ Memory and register values should be in hexadecimal format. 

❖ Each row in the memory table consists of 16 columns, each of 1 byte. The row indicates the starting offset. Both the 
starting offset and the columns are represented with hexadecimal values. 

❖ You are supposed to debug each question in Visual Studio after filling the tables. 

❖ Submit a PDF File with the naming format 23i-1234_Section_(AI,DS)

 ❖ If you find any ERROR in the program highlight the error and write the justification for the error. You must 
understand ERROR carefully. After identifying the error, you will ignore it by commenting it out and running the 
program. Also, the register values corresponding to the erroneous statements must be left blank. For example:
; mov al, 256 ERROR: 256 is out of range for an 8-bit register like `AL`. It should be within 0-255.

 ❖ Data Declarations highlighted in yellow must be replaced as instructed below.

 ❖ Late submission will not be accepted and if any student fail to submit the hard copy or scan of the assignment 50% marks will be deducted from his obtained marks.

courseWork.title: COAL: Assignment 1

Dear Students Please consider the following instructions related to Assignment# 1

Please first of all read the instruction of the assignment mentioned at the first page. You are required to understand "How you will consider your roll number as a Byte, Word and Double Word" for the given questions. Furthermore you also need to understand the pattern of your name required to be used as string.

You are required to solve every question by hand and show each step of the solution

As the complete assignment is based on your Roll Number so there is Zero percent probability of similarity in the questions. If any question or any single part of the assignment seems plagiarized either from any student or from any AI tool the assignment will not considered for grading. 

The submission deadline is 22nd Feb (Saturday). You are required to submit the soft copy and hard copy of the assignment as well.

If your Class is not scheduled on Friday you may submit your assignment earlier to your relevant course instructor and can submit the soft copy (scanned form) on GCR link on said date.

Submission of invalid file, incomplete file will not be considered for grading, even in case you have completed the assignment later and submitted  complete hard copy.

If you have submitted the  hard copy of the assignment and forgot to upload scan copy of the assignment still your assignment will not be graded.

Please find attached the case study Healthcare.gov. Your task is to review this case study and answer the following questions critically:

Highlight technical flaws in the initial rollout of HealthCare.gov.
How does a lack of stakeholder involvement contribute to the failure of HealthCare.gov?

Thank you

Instructions for final exam.
The final exam consists of 2 parts. Part-I consists of 91 MCQs (91 marks) and is of 1 hour duration. Part-II is 120 marks and 2 hours. There's no negative marking in the MCQs section. Cutting/Erasing/Overwriting will lead to cancellation of the question.
Please note the exam has been intentionally designed to be slightly lengthy. So try to keep up the pace throughout. 
The students must not ask any questions from the invigilators. If you think any information is missing in the questions, make an appropriate assumption, write it along the answer, and attempt it accordingly. In coding-based questions please do not assume that any data structure is already implemented and available to you unless already exclusively mentioned in the question.
The MCQs answer sheet is attached please note the roll no. filling method, write the roll no. in the provided space and fill the relevant circles as well. Be careful in the roll no section, otherwise marks may be deducted. A sample MCQs answer sheet is attached herewith for your understanding. 
Good Luck

Topics for Final Exam:
1) Introduction to data structures
2) Abstract data types
3) Complexity theory (time Complexity)
4) Arrays, Address translation
5) Sorting/Searching algorithms
6) Lists, Linked list implementation using arrays and pointers
7) Linked List Variations (Single Linked List, Double Linked List, Single Circular List, Double Circular List)
8) Stacks & its applications and implementation using arrays and List
9) Queue and implementation using arrays and List
10) Trees: Tree data structure definition and basic terminologies
11) Trees: Tree Traversal, Expression trees
12) Trees: Binary Search Trees
13) Trees: AVL Trees
14) Trees: Binary Heap
15) Trees Implementations (all variations of Trees)
16) Hashing and collision Techniques (implementation included)
17) Graphs: Definitions and Basic terminology
18) Graphs: Traversal (implementation included)
19) Graphs: Minimum spanning trees
20) Graphs: Shortest path trees (implementation included)

Paper Pattern includes: 1) MCQs, 2) Short Questions, 3) Long Questions

🚀 Exciting Summer Internship Opportunities at The Neuron Gorge! 🔬🧠

We’re thrilled to announce that The Neuron Gorge is now accepting applications for our Summer Internship Program 2025! If you're passionate about AI and eager to work on real-world problems, this is your chance to shine. 🌟

💼 Available Internship Positions:

🔹 Natural Language Processing & Machine Learning (3 Positions)
Work on language models, text classification, sentiment analysis, prompt engineering, and other NLP tasks. You’ll explore how machines understand and generate human language using deep learning, transformers, and large language models.

🔹 Computer Vision (3 Positions)
Dive into image classification, object detection, and vision transformers. You'll work on real datasets, ranging from medical imaging to visual surveillance and scene understanding.

📍 Location: Remote (with optional in-person meetups for local interns)
🕒 Duration: 6–8 weeks (flexible based on mutual availability)

📈 What You’ll Gain:
Hands-on experience with real-world datasets and challenges
Mentorship from experienced researchers
A certificate of completion and a chance to be featured on our platforms
Possible long-term collaboration for research or publication

courseWorkMaterials.title: Regarding Final Exam
courseWorkMaterials.description:
Dear Students, I hope you’re doing well. Following is the paper pattern:
Question 1 (Recursion) [12 marks]  
Question 2 [10 marks] - This question is taken from the quiz/quiz syllabus with minor modification
Question 3 (Problem Solving) [15 marks]
Question 4 (Theoretical short questions) [2*5 = 10] - There will be no unseen question, prepare yourself from links mentioned in "Theoretical Concepts in OOP" material, that is already uploaded on GCR. You will be required to type the answers in txt file. I will share couple of more links by tomorrow.
Question 5 (Combination of concepts like Classes, DMA, Encapsulation, Operator Overloading etc.) [30 marks]
Question 6 (Polymorphism)  [30 marks]
Question 7 [10 marks] - This question is taken from your lab task 
Question 8 [8 marks] - This question is taken from OOP Lab Mid Exam (Sec A,B,C), solution is already been shared. (Stack not included)
Exam looks lengthy but actually it's not. Skeleton code will be provided to you. It will not be complex, just constructors, destructors, main and getters/setters. Final exam weightage is 50 absolutes, and there will be NO SCALING.
There will be no binary marking. However, marking gonna be strict. I am very much concerned about the correctness of program in each question. One correct answer worth more than half attempted 4 questions. Incase of incorrect answer, it won't be zero but there will be massive deduction of marks. Prepare yourself accordingly. 

Important: There is a huge difference between is-a and has-a relationship. Many students inherited PowerUp/PowerDown/Ball/Brick classes in Game class when you were working on a project. Try to understand, for example Ball and Game doesn't make a parent child relationship. Game isn't a subtype of Ball. According to the project rubric you obtained marks, but in OOP Lab final it will be considered incorrect. Learn OOP & significance of OOP. When to make struct and why should I make classes? In a particular scenario why composition why not aggregation or inheritance. Identify the relationships correctly.

For a better understanding of the concept of "Exactly one", consider this example: "Everyone has exactly one best friend". This can be formally expressed as ∀x ∃y(BF(x, y) ∧ ∀z((z ≠ y) → ¬BF(x, z))). 

In English it will be read as: For every person x, there exists a unique person y who is x's best friend, and no other person z can be x's best friend if z is not y.

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=2iFzzor5Pfs

courseWorkMaterials.description:
If you complete the question correctly, please email me the .cpp file. Make sure to test your code on variety of inputs, including negative integers & zeros.

Question: Array Combinations for Target Sum using Dynamic Memory Allocation (DMA) in C++
You are tasked with writing a C++ program that dynamically allocates memory for an array of integers based on user input. The program should then find and display all possible combinations of elements from the array that add up to a given target sum.
Enter the size of the array: 8
Enter the elements of the array:
1 1 3 2 5 4 1 6 
Enter the target sum: 5

Original Array: 1 1 3 2 5 4 1 6
Target Sum: 5

Combinations:
5
4 & 1
3 & 2
3 & 1 & 1
2 & 1 & 1 & 1

Question
Create a program to arrange eight asterisks (*) on an 8x8 grid in such a way that no two asterisks share the same row, column, or diagonal. Develop an algorithm to achieve this unique arrangement on the grid, considering both horizontal, vertical, and diagonal constraints. Aim for an optimal distribution of the asterisks across the 8x8 matrix.Your solution must be scalable to 16 sterics in 16*16 array, 32 sterics in 32*32 array, 64 sterics in 64*64 array. Your code should be generic & flexible and remember to allocate & deallocate the memory. The objective is to create a flexible solution that adapts to different board dimensions while maintaining the constraint that no asterisk shares the same row, column, or diagonal with another.

List of ideas for meme generation

Here are some meme ideas to get you started:
1. Expectation vs Reality: Create a meme showing a glamorous expectation versus a
hilariously mundane reality. For example, a picture of a gourmet meal expectation next to
a reality of burnt toast.
2. Monday vs Friday Contrast the emotions or situations experienced on Monday
versus Friday. This could be anything from a sleepy Monday morning face compared to a
happy Friday dance.
3. Pet Owner Problems: Depict common struggles pet owners face in a humorous way.
Think about scenarios like trying to make the bed with a cat sitting on it or waking up to
your dog stealing your pillow.
4. Zoom Call Fails: Capture the awkwardness and mishaps that often occur during
online meetings or video calls. This could include someone forgetting to mute themselves
while doing something embarrassing in the background.
5. Parenting Realities: Illustrate the difference between parents' expectations of raising
children versus the chaotic reality. This might involve a serene image of parents sipping
coffee versus a chaotic scene of toys strewn everywhere.
6. Gym Dilemmas: Create memes that poke fun at common gym experiences or excuses
people use to avoid exercising. For instance, a meme showing someone enthusiastically
planning their gym routine on Sunday night, then hitting the snooze button repeatedly on
Monday morning.
7. Tech Support Woes; Show the frustration of dealing with tech support in a humorous
way. This could involve a meme of someone screaming into a phone while a robot voice
repeats, Your call is important to us."
8. Weather Mood Swings; Capture the unpredictability of weather changes in a meme.
This could be a series of images showing someone leaving the house dressed for sunny
weather, only to be caught in a sudden downpour.

9. Cooking Catastrophes: Highlight the comical mishaps that occur in the kitchen. This
might include a meme of someone proudly presenting a Pinterest-worthy dish next to a
reality of burnt cookies or a collapsed cake.
10. social Media Vs Reality; Contrast the carefully curated images people post on social
media with the less glamorous reality behind the scenes. This could involve a side-by-
side comparison of a perfectly posed Instagram photo versus the chaos happening just
outside the frame.

Title: Meme Master Workout 25 minutes 
Objective: Create your own hilarious memes while exercising your creativity and humor
muscles!
1. Pen and paper or a digital device for jotting down ideas
2. Internet access for meme templates and inspiration
1. Warm-up: Spend 5-10 minutes browsing popular meme websites or social media
platforms to get into the meme-making mindset. Take note of trending memes and
formats that catch your eye.
2. Brainstorm: Set a timer for 5 minutes and brainstorm meme ideas. Think about current
events, pop culture references, relatable situations, or anything else that sparks your
creativity. Write down as many ideas as possible, no matter how silly or outrageous they
may seem.
3. Stretch Your Creativity: Choose one of your brainstormed ideas and develop it into a
full-fledged meme. Consider different angles, captions, and imagery that could make
your meme stand out. Don't be afraid to think outside the box!
4. Exercise Your Funny Bone: Once you have a solid concept, it's time to craft your
meme. Use meme-making tools or software to bring your idea to life. If youre feeling
adventurous, try creating a custom drawing or illustration for a truly unique meme.

5. Share and Review: Share your meme with friends, family, or online communities to get
feedback and reactions. Remember, the goal is to bring joy and laughter.

courseWork.title: Final Project
courseWork.description:
Purpose of the final Project:
The purpose of the project is to create awareness among society regarding social and current issues. In social sciences, Society is considered the lab for observations and experiments for the students of social sciences. Therefore, the students are required to visit random places and societies to observe the social issues and opinions of the people. Intellectually, it is a healthy activity for the students of social sciences to learn the art of communication and fieldwork through this project. Besides this, the students can create awareness among people regarding social issues. 

Procedure: 
All the students are divided into groups. Each group has to make a video (Documentary) of 10 to 20 minutes. The content of the video would be based on the assigned topics. The group members are instructed to ask topic-related questions from random people to fulfill the requirements of the project. First of all, the group members have to introduce themselves in the video and then continue the video by asking questions from random people. Once you are done with the task, conclude your video with the experience that you get from the project and also mention whether the activity was helpful or not. All the students have to participate in the project and video.

Instructions for the Project:
1. First of all, make at least 15-20 questions regarding the assigned topic and show them to your instructor.
2. Select an open area (Marketplace, Parks, shopping malls, universities, and institutions) for your project and avoid going to rural areas.
3. Before starting the interview, introduce yourself with your institutional background and the purpose of the project so that people feel comfortable answering your questions.
4. Do not make fun of people if they are not able to answer your questions.
5. Some people would get emotional or aggressive during interviews, in such cases, no need to be panic just leave them and move on.
6. Do not use unethical language during your interviews.
7. Be professional while asking your questions.
8. Keep in mind that the purpose of the project is to create awareness about social and current issues in Pakistan amongst people.
9. As it is a trend on social media (TikTok, Facebook, YouTube) so most people will not be ready to answer your questions. Assure them that the purpose of recording video is an academic activity and it won’t be published or shared anywhere.
10. Avoid asking personal questions.

How to Start the Project?
Step 1: Make a group of 5-7 students
Step 2: Select a group leader who will be in contact with the instructor regarding the project activity.
Step 3: The group leader will assign activities to the students.
Step 4: Decide a day, time, and place for the project activity and inform your colleagues.
Step 5: Edit the video and make it a short documentary. Add your names to the video with credits. Give a title to your documentary and upload it on GCR. 
Note: All the group members are strictly instructed to coordinate with the group leader.

Deadline: 15 November 2023

courseWorkMaterials.title: Practice Questions for String
courseWorkMaterials.description:
1- Design a password validation C++ program for a user registration system. The password must adhere to the following criteria. Take password as string input.
At least 8 characters long.
Contains a mix of uppercase and lowercase letters.
Includes at least one numeric digit.
Contains at least one special character (e.g., @, #, $, %).
2- Write a C++ program that takes a string as input and returns the reversed version of the string. Do not use any built-in reverse functions. (without using temporary array)
Input: "Hello, World!"
Output: "!dlroW ,olleH"

3- Write a C++ program that takes a sentence as input and displays the number of words in it. Assume that words are separated by spaces, and there are no leading or trailing spaces. The program should handle multiple spaces between words and ignore them while counting. Test your program with different sentences.

4- Implement a C++ program that checks if a given string is a palindrome. A palindrome is a word, phrase, number, or other sequence of characters that reads the same forward and backward.

announcements.text: Dear students, I hope you are all doing well. As you get ready for the calculus final exam, make sure to review all the topics we covered in class. The final exam for Calculus and Analytic Geometry includes 20% from Sessional-I, 30% from Sessional-II, and 50% from the material covered after Sessional-II. Therefore, it's important to focus on preparing the syllabus with the highest weightage first. We have covered all the topics in class, so practice them to achieve the best possible marks. Thank you!

Dear students, please be informed that I have uploaded all your internal assessment marks on FLEX, and the entries are now final and cannot be changed. Kindly review your marks. If you have any questions or concerns, feel free to email me or contact me at 03005789117 before 8:00 pm today. Thank you!
Dear students, tomorrow's quiz will cover trigonometric integrals (Section 8.3). Thank you!

Dear students,

I trust you are all well-prepared for tomorrow's exam. Note that the Sessional-II exam syllabus will encompass material from Exercise 3.4 to 4.8. Please follow the provided course outline, which includes all the topics we have addressed in class. Ensure thorough practice of Related rate problems, iImplicit differentiation, 1st derivative test, 2nd derivative test, Curve sketching, L'Hopital Rule, and Applied Optimization. 
Best of luck for your exam.
Dear students, please note that the submission date for Homework 04 has been extended to Tuesday, October 17, 2023. Thank you!

Dear students,

Regarding the Sessional-I exam, please remember that the syllabus remains focused up to Exercise 3.3. To perform well, concentrate on the following topics:

1. Function Domains and Ranges: Understand where functions work and the values they can take. Recognize even and odd functions and their symmetries.

2. Function Transformations: Learn how to manipulate functions through translation, scaling, and composition, and find equations for translated functions.

3. Limits and Continuity: Grasp the concepts of limits and how functions behave when they are continuous.

4. Graph Asymptotes: Identify and work with various types of asymptotes in graphs, including horizontal, vertical, and oblique asymptotes.

5. Differentiable Functions: Develop proficiency in graphing differentiable functions, finding derivatives using basic rules, and determining equations for tangent and normal lines.

6. Piecewise Functions: Understand the concept of differentiability in piecewise functions.

By focusing on these specific aspects of the topics, you'll be well-prepared for the exam.

Dear Students

Your final exam show up will be on 12-January-2023. I will share the time and venue information a day before.

Important topics for final:

1 OS scenario based question just like quiz

2 number system

3 Network topology (you should be able to design the network given in quiz 5)

4 JavaScript function (such as login code) discussed in class

5 mcqs general knowledge

6 Database lecture ( topics like data standardization, duplication etc)

7 from lecture computer networks topic exponential back off during collision. How to calculate it by formula.

Try to focus on these topics first and then the other lectures.
Paper will mostly consist of scenario based questions. So understanding of all topics is key to score good marks.
Again don't get panic by seeing the length of the questions. 
Try to find relevant information out of it and ignore the unnecessary details.

Best of luck

Important Announcement For IICT Final Exam:
Cover all syllabus of your lab (including lab tasks, assignments, and lecture slides).
You should all be well-versed with HTML, CSS, and Bootstrap code used in your project.
Utilize all the Additional IICT resources shared on GCR (including web links, videos, and JS source code).

Important topics that you should prepare are Network Topologies, Number System Conversion, OS, Database, and Network Protocols (especially Exponential Backoff).
Most of the paper will be scenario-based (You will have to solve problems based on the given scenario).
Calculator is allowed.
Ratta is not required (be clear of all of your concepts.)

This is everything you should know to prepare for your exam tomorrow. GOOD LUCK!

Dear Students
As we approach the conclusion of our syllabus, I would like to inform you about the upcoming group presentations schedule. Each presentation will be conducted in groups. Along with your presentation, you are required to submit a comprehensive report on the chosen topic. Following are the presentation guidelines:

Each group will have 10 minutes to present (So beware about the number of slides don't make too many of it), followed by a 20-minute question-and-answer session.
Marking of the presentation will be done on an individual basis; therefore,  every member of the group must actively participate in the presentation.
You have to prepare presentation slides as well, which must be submitted along with the report.
The order of presentation will be randomized, and groups should be prepared for their turn as I can call any group to present.
All students have to present in English. Remember all the skills we have learnt in presentation skills lecture and apply them to your project presentation.
There will be No retakes for missed presentations due to our limited remaining time.
PRESENTATION CONTENT:
Brief introduction about your website.
Why have you chosen specific domain(Motivation).
What problem it is likely to solve (Problem Statement).
What target audience will be benefitted from it (Target Market).
Functionality of your website. (summarized points)
Theme Selection criteria (Why you have selected certain colors does it suits your domain)
Have you inculcated responsiveness?
Would you like to develop it in a full scale product (Future direction)

As per the request of your class I am increasing the deadline to Sunday 11:59 PM. However if any group fails to submit their work (Project+ report+ presentation slides all three must be zipped and submitted to IICT semester project)
in required time limit, zero marks will be given to whole group.
